DEFINITION · qeva:1:rational@1

Rational number

Rational numbers represent ratios of integers with nonzero denominator.

editorialnumber-theory · algebra
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

Rational numbers represent ratios of integers with nonzero denominator.

EXACT

The compact statement

ℚ may be constructed from pairs (a,b)∈ℤ×(ℤ\{0}) modulo (a,b)~(c,d) iff ad=bc.

Example

(1,2) and (2,4) represent the same rational number.

Boundary / caveat

A written decimal need not be rational unless its expansion eventually repeats.

Assumptions

  • The declared field of fractions context is fixed.
